mechanism_narrative: A rising GDP indicates economic expansion, leading to increased corporate earnings and positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: GDP growth is positive but S&P 500 returns are negative in more than 40% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: If unemployment rises above 10%, it signals economic weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: Unemployment exceeds 10% but S&P 500 returns remain positive.

mechanism_narrative: When inflation (CPIAUCSL) is high and federal funds rate is low, it may lead to negative real returns, causing S&P 500 to decline over 20 days.
failure_condition: CPIAUCSL and FEDFUNDS meet the trigger but S&P 500 returns are positive.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion, rising industrial production signals continued economic growth, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: Industrial production rises but S&P 500 returns are negative.

mechanism_narrative: Increasing housing starts indicate economic expansion, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: Housing starts rise but S&P 500 returns are negative.

mechanism_narrative: Retail sales above $350 billion indicate strong consumer spending, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: Retail sales exceed $350 billion but S&P 500 returns are negative.

mechanism_narrative: When employment rises and unemployment falls, it signals a strong labor market, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: Employment rises and unemployment falls but S&P 500 returns are negative.

mechanism_narrative: In a monetary tightening cycle, low federal funds rates still support positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: Federal funds rate is low but S&P 500 returns are negative.
